research: https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/ultimate-prompting-guide-for-nano-banana — Google's guide: write a narrative, not a keyword list, in the order subject + action + location + composition + style; name the lens and depth of field, the light and the film stock ('slightly grainy', 'muted teal'); say what you want rather than what you don't ('empty street', not 'no cars'); 9:16 is supported natively; for references, give the image plus a relationship instruction ('use the attached as the structure...').

https://dev.to/googleai/getting-the-most-out-of-nano-banana-2-502k — Google AI dev post: name the light source, its colour and its quality; describe the capture device and its artefacts (noise, distortion); with a reference, say 'based on the attached' and list what must stay; try cheap low-res variations first, then upscale the best composition.

https://pages.theortusgroup.com/corpuls3-system — UK ambulance monitors (corpuls3) are fixed to the wall beside the paramedic seat, at arm's length from the stretcher, so the monitor sits high on the side wall, not on a trolley.

https://medictests.com/units/asystole-and-pea — asystole shows on the monitor as a flat or near-flat line; crews keep compressing through it, so the moment hands come off the chest is the moment someone has decided. That pause is the image.
https://eprints.kingston.ac.uk/33844/12/Quinn-T-33844-VoR.pdf — UK study with four ambulance services: CPR in a moving ambulance is a known problem; crews brace against the stretcher and grab rails.

https://www.newsshooter.com/2026/09/15/capturing-chaos-inside-the-camera-lighting-workflow-of-hbos-the-pitt/ — The Pitt (medical drama) uses hard overhead light like a real ER, plus small practicals; overhead light is unflattering on faces, and that is the point.

https://britishcinematographer.co.uk/?p=109268 (search summary, page returned 403) — the short 'Stay Calm', set inside an ambulance: the aim was a cold, sickly interior with tube lights, plus flags and lamps swung outside the vehicle to fake passing street light and siren. Moving coloured light through the windows sells 'night outside'.
attach_reference: yes, for the wide (idea 2), where the layout matters: the teal seats, the hatch to the cab and the white cupboards are quicker to copy than to describe. Tell it to use the photo for the layout and materials only, because the photo is in daylight and its signs ('MIND YOUR HEAD', no-smoking stickers) will reappear as readable text. For the two close shots the description is enough, and leaving the photo off avoids the daylight and the signs.
notes: The monitor's numbers may come back as readable digits: blur or crop them in the edit if so. The blue strobe is better added as a pulsing light in Premiere over the still or the clip than relied on in one frame. Hold the shot still for the 3 seconds; the flatline tone and the rain do the work.

prompts.idea: The monitor is the subject: the screen sharp in the foreground on a long lens, the paramedic and patient soft behind it. The verdict reads first, then the people.
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 cinematic still, night, inside a stopped UK ambulance. In the sharp foreground, a wall-mounted heart monitor's dark screen shows one unbroken flat green line, its glow the brightest thing in frame; the small figures on it fall soft and unreadable. Behind it, out of focus on an 85mm lens, a male paramedic in a plain dark-green uniform and surgical face mask leans over the black stretcher, blue-gloved hands resting motionless on an older man's chest, oxygen mask on his grey face. Hard cold ceiling strip light, blue emergency light sweeping across the white cupboards, rain beading on the rear window. Shot on 35mm film, real grain, slightly underexposed, quiet and still. Thanks.

prompts.idea: The whole room after the fight: a wide, level 24mm from the back doors, both paramedics stopped, the cab hatch and the blue light beyond. Stillness reads as a tableau.
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 cinematic still on 35mm film at night: the full rear interior of a UK ambulance, seen from the back doors on a wide 24mm lens, low and level. White walls and cupboards, teal-green seats, grab rails, and a black stretcher with straps down the centre, where an older man lies still, grey-skinned, oxygen mask on. A woman paramedic in a plain dark-green uniform and surgical face mask sits back on her heels, blue gloves lifted just off his chest; her male colleague, masked, stands frozen with one hand on the rail. On the side wall a monitor glows with one flat green line. Through the small hatch window, the driver's silhouette and pulsing blue light; rain streams down the windows. Hard cold ceiling strips, grain, underexposed, total stillness. Thanks.

prompts.idea: Hands only: looking down at the blue-gloved hands stopped on the chest, lit green by the monitor and swept by blue from the window. No faces, so it can't go wrong, and it's the most intimate of the three.
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 cinematic close-up on 35mm film, night, inside a UK ambulance. Looking down at two blue-gloved hands, one laid over the other, resting still on the centre of an older man's chest over a thin pale gown, the pushing finished. At the top of the frame, his grey chin and the edge of a clear oxygen mask. One side of the frame is washed green by the glow of a heart monitor's flat line, reflecting off the gloves and skin; a slow band of blue emergency light falls across from a rain-streaked window. The black stretcher mattress and a loose strap fill the bottom of the frame. Hard cold overhead light, deep shadow, real grain, slightly underexposed. Quiet and devastating, not gory. Thanks.
